edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across single and batched requests
edits.content: When single and batched fetching overlap, maintain a URL-keyed dictionary of fetched text. Deduplicate candidate URLs in input order and exclude URLs already successfully cached before fetching the batch. Associate returned pages with their requested URLs and build extraction evidence from successful cached results. Reuse cached text directly for subsequent extraction and quote-membership checks. Exclude FETCH_FAILED results from usable evidence. This procedure applies when the cached rendering supplies the evidence needed for the current focus; cache presence alone does not establish relevance or completeness.

additional_candidates.description: Deduplicate batch fetch targets against a URL-keyed cache and reuse stored evidence for extraction and citation validation.
Use schema-validated extraction followed by coverage, source-domain, quote-membership, and constraint checks.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, but this snapshot ends after constraint-check calls. The final code places answer serialization and readiness after refine.run, and no execution result for that completed block is visible. Earlier extraction produced five rows with no validation failures. Submission is therefore unconfirmed; the evidence does not establish a reusable failure cause or a recovery.

Both flagged batch queries returned four hits and recorded no new entities after the single search had already recorded all requested quantities. Both single and batched search were explicitly required for this demonstration. The batch supplied pages subsequently fetched successfully, so these two zero-discovery signals do not demonstrate an unproductive search loop.

The executed fetch block deduplicated batch URLs, excluded the already fetched URL, stored four usable pages, and retrieved cached text without another backend fetch. Subsequent validation used that same cache for quote membership. This supplies a concrete reusable tactic beyond the base prompt's general instruction to reuse evidence. No existing entries require updating.

Schema-validated extraction returned five rows, and the executed validation reported no failures; constraint calls also returned successfully through the last row. These are useful process successes, but the immutable base instructions already prescribe typed extraction, programmatic coverage and quote checks, and constraint recording. Another entry would duplicate that coverage, and the snapshot does not confirm final submission.
